deep.reconstruction:
Context. These notes (cote 121, 1974) set up an axiomatic 'tame topology'. There is an ambient category K of spaces, a subcategory M of 'tame' objects and maps, a final object e, and an interval object I (written I_0 when viewed in M). Earlier pages work with systems M_n of admissible subobjects of I^n subject to axioms M1, M2, M3(bis) and further axioms 1°–6°. The previous page proves that contractile diagrams can be glued using embeddings into cubes I_0^N and retractions.

This page. Grothendieck notes that axioms 5° and 6° are not easily stated in terms of the M_n. He therefore switches to a function-based presentation of the same data.

1. Function sets. Let F_n ⊂ Hom_K(I^n, I) be the set Hom_M(I_0^n, I_0) of tame functions of n variables. Axiom 6°, apparently 'every admissible set is a zero set/fibre of a tame map', means the F_n determine the M_n.

2. Axioms on the F_n.
- Define F_{m,n} ⊂ Hom_K(I^n, I^m) as the maps φ = (φ_1, …, φ_m) with every φ_i ∈ F_n.
- (F1): the projections pr_i : I^n → I lie in F_n.
- (F2): the F_{m,n} are closed under composition.
- Together, (F1) and (F2) say that (F_n) is a clone, or equivalently a Lawvere algebraic theory, inside K with I as its generic object.

3. Recovering the sets. Define M_n as the finite intersections of sets φ^{-1}(α), with φ ∈ F_n and α ∈ F_0 a point e → I. Then M_* satisfies M1 and M2. To get M3bis one needs further axioms:
- (F3): a tuple (φ_1, …, φ_m) of functions in F_n gives a map I^n → I^m (left unfinished).
- (F4a): there is a base point o ∈ F_0 such that every point α : e → I is a finite intersection ∩ φ_i^{-1}(o) with φ_i ∈ F_1. Points are 'zero sets', so all generators can be rewritten using the single value o.
- (F4b): the cross o×I ∪ I×o ⊂ I^2 lies in M_2, i.e. it is ∩ φ_i^{-1}(o) with φ_i ∈ F_2. In the real model this is the zero set of xy. It gives closure of M_n under finite unions: φ^{-1}(o) ∪ ψ^{-1}(o) = (φ,ψ)^{-1}(cross), and intersections distribute over unions.
- (F4c): there are two points ε_1, ε_2 : e → I with e ⊔ e → I mono, i.e. I is nontrivial.

4. Graph criterion. For f : X → I with X ⊂ I^n, consider the graph Γ_f ⊂ I^{n+1}. For f on all of I^n:
- 'Only if' (f ∈ F_n ⇒ Γ_f ∈ M_{n+1}) is equivalent to the diagonal Δ_I ⊂ I×I lying in M_2. This works because Γ_f = (f∘pr, pr_{n+1})^{-1}(Δ_I).
- 'If' (Γ_f ∈ M_{n+1} ⇒ f ∈ F_n) must be postulated separately.

This is the familiar principle that a function is definable iff its graph is definable, made into an explicit axiom. The purpose throughout is to axiomatize a tame category of 'polyhedra' (semi-algebraic or semi-analytic type) through an algebraic theory of tame functions on an interval rather than through families of subsets.
errors: (F3) is left incomplete on the page (only 'si φ_1…φ_m ∈ F_n d'où I^n→I^m' followed by a dash), so the M3bis condition is never actually formulated.
In (F4a) the quantifier should be over points α ∈ F_0 (maps e→I), with the φ_i in F_1; the transcription's 'α ∈ F_1' is inconsistent with 'α : e → I'.

As defined, the M_n are closed under finite intersections and (given F4b) finite unions, but not complements. They model closed/zero-set families, not a Boolean algebra of definable sets. Whether this matches the earlier axioms M1–M3 cannot be checked from this page.

The graph criterion is stated for f : X → I with X ⊂ I^n, but the 'il faut' argument via Δ_I only directly handles f defined on all of I^n (or on X ∈ M_n by intersecting). Partial functions need a convention not given here.

ideas.what: Presenting a tame/definable structure by its sets of n-ary tame functions I^n→I, closed under projections and composition
ideas.modern_name: Clone / Lawvere algebraic theory of definable functions; function-based presentation of an o-minimal-type structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lawvere (1963) for algebraic theories; van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1984–86) and Shiota for o-minimal/tame structures
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984); this axiomatization is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Admissible sets as finite intersections of zero sets φ^{-1}(o) of tame functions; points are zero sets
ideas.modern_name: Zero-set (Z-set) generation of a lattice of closed definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gillman–Jerison zero sets; semialgebraic geometry: closed semialgebraic sets are zero sets of continuous semialgebraic functions)

ideas.what: Closure under finite unions reduced to the single condition that the cross o×I ∪ I×o is a zero set (the role of the product xy)
ideas.modern_name: Union axiom via pulling back the coordinate cross

ideas.what: f tame iff its graph is admissible; 'only if' is equivalent to the diagonal being admissible, 'if' must be postulated

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins recasting his axioms for tame topology as an algebraic theory (clone) of tame functions on an interval object I, with sets recovered as zero loci. Unlike o-minimality (sets first) or C^∞-ring/Lawvere-theory approaches (no tameness), this is an intrinsic categorical axiomatization of tame geometry. The page leaves (F3)/M3bis unfinished and does not state the analogues of 5°/6°.
missed.quote: Il ne semble pas que 5° et 6° s'expriment de façon simple en termes des M_n. Mais on va en profiter pour reformuler les données ainsi.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A presentation of o-minimal or tame structures as Lawvere theories with an interval object, with zero-set axioms, is close in spirit to later work on categorical o-minimality and on synthetic/C^∞-ring approaches. It shows Grothendieck had a theory-of-functions viewpoint on tame topology in 1974, a decade before o-minimality.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual facts (zero-set generation, the graph criterion, union via the cross) are routine. What is of mild historical interest is that in 1974 Grothendieck was axiomatizing tame topology through a clone/Lawvere theory of tame functions on an interval. This is unpublished and predates o-minimality, but the page is fragmentary and the content is fairly standard once the viewpoint is chosen.
transcription_corrections: '(e×I ; I×e)' is preceded by a struck-through word that reads like 'Sup' (union): the set meant is the union of the two axes o×I ∪ I×o, not a pair.
In (F4a) the image suggests '∀α ∈ F_0' (points), with the {+∈F_0+} annotation attached to o; the φ_i are in F_1.
'Hom_K(I^n, I)' carries a subscript 𝒦 (the ambient category), and 'Hom_M(I_0^n, I_0)' has subscript ℳ.
'M3 bis (ou un fait)' is unclear; possibly '(ou mieux fait)'.
'(F1) F_n contient les pr_i : I^n → I' is an interlinear insertion replacing a struck first (F1).
